newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan, Germany seek extended air links -reports.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan, Germany seek extended air links -reports.

text.p: Taiwan and Germany are exploring ways to extend mutual air links, including a new Taipei-Berlin route that could upset communist China, Taipei newspapers said on Thursday.

A delegation of German parliament members and executives plans to visit Taiwan at the end of February to discuss the possible opening of Taipei-Berlin and Taipei-Hamburg routes, several dailies quoted aviation sources as saying.
Taiwan carrier EVA Airways, a unit of shipping giant Evergreen Marine, has been actively promoting such links, the reports said.

Germany, which recognises the communist government in Beijing rather than Taiwan's exiled Republic of China, in the past had refused to let Taiwan carriers fly to the capital Berlin to avoid China's likely protests, the reports said.

Taiwan, seen by Beijing as a renegade province since a civil war split them in 1949, has openly asked to buy submarines from Germany to bolster its defences against China's modernising navy -- a deal Beijing vehemently opposes.
Taiwan transport officials cautiously welcomed the private aviation initiative, but said it required further discussion between German and Taiwan authorities, the reports said.
Taiwan's civil aviation administration and airlines offices were closed for the lunar new year holiday and officials and executives could not be reached for comment.
Despite intimate bilateral trade and investment links, only Taiwan's China Airlines flies directly to Germany with its regular service to Frankfurt.

German flagship airline Lufthansa dropped a weekly non-stop Frankfurt-Taipei service in June 1996 as unprofitable, shifting its focus across the Taiwan strait to China's booming industrial and financial capital Shanghai.
The existing aviation pact between Taiwan and Germany was signed in May 1993 by two private groups due to the absence of formal ties between Taipei and Berlin.

China has expressed anger at a reported secret aviation pact between Taiwan and Cambodia, which like Germany recognises Beijing rather than Taipei, saying Beijing must be allowed to approve such agreements.

"The Chinese side is firmly opposed...that those countries having diplomatic relations with China establish official air links with Taiwan," said a statement issued on Wednesday by the Chinese Embassy in Phnom Penh.
"In case those countries intend to establish non-governmental air links with Taiwan, they must get permission from the Chinese government beforehand," it added.
